issue_context.title: Panic after unpivot of DataFrame with pl.string_cache_enabled()
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl
import polars.selectors as cs

def reproducer():
    df = pl.DataFrame({
        "index": [0, 1],
        "series1": pl.Series(["a", "b"], dtype=pl.Categorical),
        "series2": pl.Series(["b", "c"], dtype=pl.Categorical),
    })
    df = df.unpivot(cs.categorical(), index="index")
    print(df)

pl.enable_string_cache()
reproducer()

```


### Log output

```shell
thread '<unnamed>' panicked at crates/polars-core/src/chunked_array/logical/categorical/revmap.rs:103:42:
called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
PanicException                            Traceback (most recent call last)
/tmp/ipykernel_311/2485256769.py in ?()
     16     df = df.unpivot(cs.categorical(), index="index")
     17     print(df)
     18 
     19 pl.enable_string_cache()
---> 20 reproducer()

/tmp/ipykernel_311/2485256769.py in ?()
     13         "series2": pl.Series(["b", "c"], dtype=pl.Categorical),
     14 
     15     })
     16     df = df.unpivot(cs.categorical(), index="index")
---> 17     print(df)

/opt/conda/lib/python3.11/site-packages/polars/dataframe/frame.py in ?(self)
   1174     def __str__(self) -> str:
-> 1175         return self._df.as_str()

PanicException: called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value
```


### Issue description

I am seeing a panic after an unpivot of a dataframe with `pl.Categorical` dtypes with the polars string cache enabled. This problem does not occur if the string cache is not enabled or if using string dtypes during the unpivot operation.

While chasing this down, I noticed that after the unpivot, I could sometimes access portions of the resulting DataFrame using things like `head(5)`, but that operations that would print, store, or access the full DataFrame would panic. It suggests to me that after the unpivot, a particular category perhaps did not have a mapping in the string cache that existed before the unpivot.

### Expected behavior

I expect no panic to happen and the DataFrame to look equivalent to the output of `reproduce()` without `pl.enable_string_cache()`
